statement: A rectangle measures 8 cm by 6 cm. The midpoints of its four sides are joined in order to form a rhombus. What is the area of the rhombus?

choices.misconception: I thought the rhombus was a quarter of the rectangle.
I worked out each side of the rhombus is 5 cm and then gave the perimeter, 4 times 5.
I found the rhombus side is 5 cm and squared it, treating the rhombus as if it were a square.
I multiplied the two diagonals, 8 and 6, and forgot to halve the product.

hints: Look at the four corner triangles that are cut off.
Area by dissection: the rhombus and the four corner triangles together make the rectangle. Compare one corner triangle with the quarter of the rectangle it sits in.
Each corner triangle has legs 4 and 3, so its area is 6, and there are four of them.

solutions.reliable: Each cut-off corner is a right triangle with legs 4 cm and 3 cm, area 6 square cm. Four of them make 24, so the rhombus is 48 minus 24, which is 24 square cm. The transferable idea: when a shape is awkward, find its area as the whole minus simple pieces.
solutions.elegant: Each quarter of the rectangle is split by a side of the rhombus into two equal triangles, one inside and one outside. So the rhombus is exactly half the rectangle, 24 square cm.

whyOnTest: Midpoint shapes are a dissection classic: one cut shows the rhombus is half the rectangle, and the distractors catch side-squared and perimeter slips.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
